report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true and supported by strong scientific evidence**. High-quality, randomized, placebo-controlled trials demonstrate that add-on (adjunctive) pharmaceutical cannabidiol (CBD) significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome.

### Scientific Evidence
* **Landmark Clinical Trial:** A pivotal randomized, double-blind trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated 120 children and young adults with drug-resistant Dravet syndrome. Over a 14-week treatment period, monthly convulsive seizures dropped from a median of 12.4 to 5.9 in the cannabidiol group (a ~39% median reduction), compared to a decrease from 14.9 to 14.1 in the placebo group.
* **Dose-Ranging Trials:** A subsequent phase 3 trial published in *JAMA Neurology* evaluated doses of 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day, confirming that both doses produced significantly greater reductions in convulsive seizure frequency compared to placebo.
* **Regulatory Approval:** Based on these clinical trials, the U.S. FDA approved Epidiolex (a purified oral cannabidiol formulation) specifically for treating seizures associated with Dravet syndrome.
* **Systematic Reviews:** Meta-analyses of pediatric epilepsy studies consistently confirm that adjunctive cannabidiol yields clinically meaningful reductions in convulsive seizure burden.

### Sources
* *The New England Journal of Medicine*: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618
* *JAMA Neurology*: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458
* Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis (PubMed Central): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13196805/
* U.S. FDA Drug Prescribing Information: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210365lbl.pdf
